database_summary: This is an e‑commerce dataset (SQLite) focused on orders, customers, sellers, products, order items, payments, and reviews plus geolocation and product category translations. Tables capture current descriptive attributes (customers, sellers, products), event/history records (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews) and dense geolocation points. Common keys: order_id, product_id, customer_id, seller_id, and zip code prefixes. Some tables (olist_order_items, olist_order_payments, olist_order_reviews) are at a finer grain than orders and can multiply when joined to orders.

accepted.name: orders_enriched_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  COALESCE(p_first.payment_type, p_agg.most_common_payment_type) AS payment_type,
  COALESCE(p_first.payment_installments, p_agg.payment_installments_mode) AS payment_installments,
  COALESCE(p_first.payment_value, p_agg.total_payment_value) AS payment_value,
  oi_agg.items_count,
  oi_agg.items_price_total,
  oi_agg.items_freight_total
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    MIN(payment_sequential) AS first_seq
  FROM olist_order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) p_first_key
  ON p_first_key.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_payments p_first
  ON p_first.order_id = p_first_key.order_id
  AND p_first.payment_sequential = p_first_key.first_seq
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS items_count,
    SUM(price) AS items_price_total,
    SUM(freight_value) AS items_freight_total
  FROM olist_order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) oi_agg
  ON oi_agg.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value,
    -- mode approximated by choosing the payment_type with max count per order
    (SELECT payment_type FROM (
       SELECT payment_type, COUNT(*) AS cnt
       FROM olist_order_payments op2
       WHERE op2.order_id = op.order_id
       GROUP BY payment_type
       ORDER BY cnt DESC
       LIMIT 1
    )) AS most_common_payment_type,
    (SELECT payment_installments FROM (
       SELECT payment_installments, COUNT(*) AS cnt
       FROM olist_order_payments op3
       WHERE op3.order_id = op.order_id
       GROUP BY payment_installments
       ORDER BY cnt DESC
       LIMIT 1
    )) AS payment_installments_mode
  FROM olist_order_payments op
  GROUP BY order_id
) p_agg
  ON p_agg.order_id = o.order_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-order enriched with customer, primary payment (first payment_sequential per order), aggregated order-level price measures (sum of item prices and freight), and delivery/approval timestamps. Useful as a starting denormalized orders table for funnel, lifecycle, geographies, and revenue analyses. | Use for: Order lifecycle and funnel (time to approve/deliver); Order revenue and payment method breakdowns; Customer-level order aggregations (join this CTE then group by customer); Analysis of orders with vs without payments or items

accepted.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  p.product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state
FROM olist_order_items oi
LEFT JOIN olist_products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN olist_sellers s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
accepted.description: One row per order item (order_id, order_item_id) with product and seller descriptive attributes joined in. Keeps item-level pricing and shipping fields. Useful for item-level revenue, seller performance, product-category sales, and shipping analyses. | Use for: Item-level revenue and margin analysis; Top products or categories by sales or quantity; Seller-level fulfillment and shipping performance; Product sizing/weight impact on freight

accepted.name: orders_reviewed
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.review_id,
  r.order_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp
FROM olist_order_reviews r
accepted.description: One-row-per-order for orders that have reviews, joining review attributes and timestamps. Useful to analyze review scores over time, correlate delivery dates with review score, or compute review conversion rates when joined to orders. | Use for: Distribution of review_score by product/category/region; Text analysis of review_comment_message/title; Time between delivery and review creation

accepted.name: product_dimensions_normalized
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  CAST(product_name_lenght AS REAL) AS product_name_lenght,
  CAST(product_description_lenght AS REAL) AS product_description_lenght,
  CAST(product_photos_qty AS REAL) AS product_photos_qty,
  CAST(product_weight_g AS REAL) AS product_weight_g,
  CAST(product_length_cm AS REAL) AS product_length_cm,
  CAST(product_height_cm AS REAL) AS product_height_cm,
  CAST(product_width_cm AS REAL) AS product_width_cm,
  (COALESCE(product_length_cm,0) * COALESCE(product_height_cm,0) * COALESCE(product_width_cm,0)) AS volumetric_size_cm3
FROM olist_products
accepted.description: Canonicalized product dimension rows with numeric casts and a computed volumetric_size_cm3 to aid size-based analyses. Useful when measuring shipping volume, normalizing nulls, or joining product metrics to sales. | Use for: Size/weight effects on freight costs; Filtering products by physical dimensions; Category-level average product dimensions

accepted.name: geolocation_zip_centroid
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  COUNT(*) AS sample_count,
  MAX(geolocation_city) AS geolocation_city,
  MAX(geolocation_state) AS geolocation_state
FROM olist_geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Aggregated geolocation by geolocation_zip_code_prefix producing average lat/lng and sample_count. Use to approximate a centroid per zip prefix for mapping or distance calculations when joining to customers/sellers by zip prefix. | Use for: Mapping customers/sellers to coordinates; Regional aggregations by zip prefix; Distance-based delivery analysis

accepted.name: customer_orders_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders,
  SUM(COALESCE(oi.price,0)) AS total_items_price,
  SUM(COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) AS total_freight,
  SUM(COALESCE(oi.price,0) + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) AS total_spent,
  MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_order_date,
  MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_order_date
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN olist_order_items oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id
accepted.description: Customer-level aggregates computed from orders and order_items: total_orders, total_items, total_spent (items price + freight), first_order_date, last_order_date. Useful for RFM, cohorting, lifetime value, and retention analyses. | Use for: Customer lifetime value and RFM; Cohort retention and repeat purchase analysis; Segment customers by spend or recency

accepted.name: orders_ranked_by_purchase
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS purchase_rank_desc
FROM olist_orders o
accepted.description: Orders with a rank per customer ordered by purchase timestamp descending (latest_order_rank = 1 means most recent). Useful to select latest N orders per customer or compute recency features. | Use for: Select latest order(s) per customer; Recency-based segmentation; Temporal cohorting and churn analysis

accepted.name: seller_monthly_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  seller_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m-01', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month_start,
  SUM(COALESCE(oi.price,0) + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0)) AS monthly_revenue,
  SUM(SUM(COALESCE(oi.price,0) + COALESCE(oi.freight_value,0))) OVER (PARTITION BY seller_id ORDER BY strftime('%Y-%m-01', o.order_purchase_timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_revenue
FROM olist_order_items oi
LEFT JOIN olist_orders o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY seller_id, strftime('%Y-%m-01', o.order_purchase_timestamp)
accepted.description: Monthly running totals of revenue per seller. Produces seller/month level rows with month_start, monthly_revenue and running_total_revenue to analyze growth and time trends per seller. | Use for: Seller growth and cumulative revenue; Monthly sales seasonality per seller; Compare running totals across sellers

accepted.name: product_category_translation_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english
FROM olist_products p
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
accepted.description: Products left-joined to the category translation lookup to expose English category names alongside original category. Useful for readable category reports and grouping across translated categories. | Use for: Category-level sales in English; Mapping local categories to standardized labels; Joinable product catalogs for reporting
